body_text: InspireMD Appoints Carotid Intervention Commercial Leader Kathleen Kennedy as Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing July 30, 2026 PDF Version Ms. Kennedy returns to InspireMD having previously served as Sales Director supporting the initial U.S. launch of CGuard Prime MIAMI, July 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- InspireMD, Inc. (Nasdaq: NSPR) (“InspireMD” or the “Company”), developer of the CGuard® Prime carotid stent system for the prevention of stroke, today announced the appointment of accomplished commercial leader Kathleen Kennedy as Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing, reporting to CEO Marvin Slosman. Ms. Kennedy brings more than 30 years of medical device sales leadership experience, including significant expertise in carotid intervention and carotid stenting. Having previously led regional sales efforts supporting the U.S. launch of CGuard Prime, she returns to InspireMD with deep relationships across the vascular, neurovascular and cardiovascular physician communities, as well as extensive experience working with health systems that are key to driving adoption of carotid therapies. “Kathy’s appointment reflects our continued commitment to building a highly talented and productive commercial team in anticipation of the planned U.S. commercialization of the CGuard platform, and I am very pleased to welcome her back to InspireMD,” stated Marvin Slosman, Chief Executive Officer. “As we prepare for the potential U.S. approval and commercial relaunch of the CGuard platform, including CGuard Prime 80cm for TCAR procedures, Kathy's deep expertise in carotid intervention, proven commercial leadership and established relationships throughout the field make her invaluable to our U.S. commercial organization and scaling our commercial growth.” “I have seen firsthand the impact CGuard and its proprietary MicroNet mesh technology can have for patients,” said Ms. Kennedy. “The strength of the clinical data, combined with the significant opportunity in the U.S. carotid intervention market, made the decision to return to InspireMD an easy one. I am excited to work with our commercial organization, physician partners and hospital customers to expand access to this important technology.” Throughout her career, Ms. Kennedy has held commercial leadership positions in cardiovascular, vascular and neurovascular medical technologies, building extensive experience in physician engagement, market development, and sales execution. Ms. Kennedy re-joins InspireMD from Omniscient Neurotechnology, where she served briefly as Vice President of Sales for North America. Prior to that, she served as Sales Director at InspireMD, as Senior Area Director at Silk Road Medical, and as Chief Commercial Officer at CAE Healthcare (now Elevate Healthcare). Earlier in her career, Ms. Kennedy held commercial positions of increasing responsibility at several healthcare companies, including Cordis, Biomet, Guidant Corporation (now Boston Scientific), and Angiodynamics. She earned a BA in Communications Studies from Northern Illinois University. About InspireMD, Inc. InspireMD seeks to utilize its proprietary MicroNet™ mesh technology to make its products the industry standard for carotid stenting by providing outstanding acute results and durable, stroke-free long-term outcomes. InspireMD’s common stock is quoted on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol NSPR. We routinely post information that may be important to investors on the Company’s website. title: 71% of Homeowners Are Open to Outreach Based on Home Condition, New PGM Solutions Research Finds
summary: New research with Ascend2 explores homeowner project plans, contractor selection, spending expectations, and why relevance matters in home improvement marketing. TAMPA, Fla., [June 17, 2026] — PGM Solutions today released new research showing homeowners are highly receptive to relevant home services outreach, particularly when it reflects factors like the age or condition of their home.
body_text: New research with Ascend2 explores homeowner project plans, contractor selection, spending expectations, and why relevance matters in home improvement marketing. TAMPA, Fla., [June 17, 2026] — PGM Solutions today released new research showing homeowners are highly receptive to relevant home services outreach, particularly when it reflects factors like the age or condition of their home. Conducted in partnership with Ascend2, the study surveyed more than 1,500 U.S. homeowners to better understand home improvement plans, contractor selection, spending expectations, and the factors influencing homeowner response to marketing. According to the research, 71% of homeowners say they are open to hearing from home service businesses with offers tied to the age or condition of their home. Another 66% say they would likely work with a company that contacted them when service was needed, reinforcing the importance of timing and relevance in home improvement marketing. The study also points to continued demand for home improvement services. Eighty-eight percent of homeowners plan a home improvement or repair project in the next 12 months, while 83% completed at least one significant project in the last three years. More than one-quarter (28%) expect to spend more than $10,000 on projects in the coming year. Additional findings include: 71% of homeowners hire professionals for at least some home improvement work 73% cite cost as the biggest reason for delaying projects, while 27% say finding a contractor they trust is a challenge Recommendations from friends and family (55%) and online search (45%) remain the leading ways homeowners find service providers Price matters, but trust signals such as local reputation, recommendations, reviews, and quality of work heavily influence final hiring decisions The findings suggest homeowners are not tuning out marketing altogether. Instead, they are more likely to respond to outreach that feels relevant to what may actually be happening with their home and arrives at the right moment. “Homeowners are telling marketers something important: relevance matters,” said Michelle Taves, Group GM of PGM Solutions. “Consumers are far more open to outreach when it reflects what may actually be happening with their home and arrives at the right time. The opportunity is not simply reaching more homeowners. It is understanding who may need what and when.” The research highlights a growing opportunity for marketers in roofing, windows, HVAC, restoration, plumbing, remodeling, and home services to better align outreach with homeowner needs and likely project timing. Homeowners report that maintenance needs, comfort, home value, weather-related concerns, and household changes all influence home improvement decisions, creating new opportunities for more relevant engagement. Through Home Factors, PGM Solutions helps marketers better understand property-related signals tied to both the interior and exterior of the home, alongside household and behavioral insights, helping brands identify when outreach may feel more timely and relevant. The full 2026 Home Improvement Marketing Report is available for download at https://porchgroupmedia.com/inbound/2026-home-improvement-marketing-report/ . About PGM Solutions PGM Solutions helps brands identify and reach high-intent consumers through its Factors suite of audience targeting solutions. People Factors provides consumer and household insights tied to life stage, demographics, and behavior. Home Factors provides exclusive property-level intelligence tied to both the interior and exterior of the home, helping marketers better understand what may be happening with a home and when outreach may matter most. Built to support audience targeting, customer acquisition, and growth, PGM Solutions helps marketers connect with consumers at more relevant moments. About Ascend2 Ascend2 specializes in creating custom research studies that empower businesses to drive demand and elevate their marketing efforts. From survey design and conceptualization to comprehensive report creation and media outreach, Ascend2 delivers end-to-end research solutions tailored to business goals. Companies partner with Ascend2 to fuel impactful marketing content, generate high-quality leads, and engage prospects using original research and data.

title: How to boost sales with AI-staged product photos
summary: Learn how to create AI-staged product photos that convert. Save time, skip the photoshoot, and boost sales with fast, pro-quality visuals.
body_text: The reality for a lot of small scale e‑commerce sellers is, traditional lifestyle photography is expensive. We're talking thousands of dollars for a single professional photoshoot. Not to mention the time it takes to plan everything, find the right location, hire models, and then wait weeks for the final images. If you're running a small brand, selling on Etsy or Shopify , or managing marketing for a growing DTC company, you need great visuals instantly and frequently, and spending that much very often is just not practical. AI product staging solves this problem. This article explores how to stage your products with AI and place them in beautiful, realistic environments that help customers visualize your products in their lives. As you read more, you’ll learn: What AI product staging is and how it compares to traditional photoshoots A step-by-step guide on using Photoroom AI staging studio How to use staged products to drive sales, and Mistakes you should avoid when staging your products with AI What is AI product staging? In the simplest terms, AI product staging is using artificial intelligence to place your product into realistic environments, without actually doing a photoshoot. Ideally, you have a photo of your product, and you want to show it in a beautiful living room, or on a beach, or in someone's hands. Instead of setting up that entire scene and taking new photos, you provide a good, clean image of your product, AI edits the image and does the heavy lifting for you. Imagine you sell handmade ceramic mugs on Etsy. You have great photos of your mugs against a white background that you took in your home studio. But you want to show how they look in real life, i.e., being held, sitting on a breakfast table, or in a cozy kitchen setting. Traditionally, you would need to do a lot of things, like: Find and rent an aesthetic kitchen or dining space Hire a photographer Maybe get a model whose hands fit her brand aesthetic Style the entire scene with props Spend a full day shooting Wait for editing and delivery That’s a lot of time and money spent. With AI product staging, you can generate multiple different lifestyle scenes in minutes and download and use them immediately. It’s important to note that staging products with AI isn’t simply “photoshopping” your product into a stock photo. Old-school mockups often look fake because getting the lighting, perspective, and integration right is really hard to do manually. AI product staging tools are specifically trained to understand both your product and the environment, creating much more realistic results. The AI handles the complex work of matching lighting conditions, creating natural shadows, adjusting color temperature, and placing your product at the right angle and scale. Why and how lifestyle product photos improve conversion A lifestyle product photo shows how your product can be used or displayed in someone's home, office, or outdoors. This is different from a transparent image , a plain product photo with a white background, or a basic mockup where you slap your logo on a generic image. When someone is shopping online, they're missing the in-store experience of picking up your product, feeling it, and imagining how it fits into their life. Lifestyle photos bridge that gap. Lifestyle photos drive conversion and increase sales because of the emotional connection that they create in the customer’s mind. Research has also shown that images showing the product in a contextual background can increase conversion rates by up to 67% compared to plain product photos . Think about it from your own experience as a shopper. When you see a candle against a white background, for example, it's just a candle. But when you see that same candle on a cozy coffee table next to a book and a warm throw blanket, suddenly you can picture it in your own living room. You're not just seeing a product anymore, you are seeing how it can look in your home. AI product staging vs. traditional photoshoots AI product staging stacks up against traditional photo shoots across every factor that matters to your business. The difference in cost is very dramatic. It is the line between "absolutely no way we can afford this" and "this is a no-brainer.” However, this comparison shows you other areas of the creative process that you need to consider when weighing your options between the two choices for product photography . AI product staging Traditional photoshoots Timeline 5-60 minutes from start to finished images 2-4 weeks (planning, shooting, editing, delivery Cost per image $0.10-$1.00 (subscription cost divided by usage) $200-$500 per usable image Setup requirements Clean product photo and internet connection Location rental, equipment, lighting setup, props Professional team needed None - you can do it yourself Photographer, potentially stylist, models, assistants Flexibility to make changes Instant, try different backgrounds in seconds Requires new shoot or expensive post-production Seasonal content creation Generate summer/winter/holiday versions instantly New photoshoot needed for each season Volume scalability Unlimited images for same monthly cost Cost increases linearly with each additional image Creative control Medium (choose from many pre-designed environments) High (full control over every element) Learning curve Minimal ( user-friendly interface, quick to master) Steep (requires photography knowledge or hiring experts) Equipment investment None Cameras, lighting, props, studio space Geographic limitations None Requires specific locations, weather dependencies Storage and organization Digital files Physical props storage, digital file management ROI for small businesses High (low cost, high impact) Low (high upfront costs may not justify small catalogs) Best use case High-volume catalogs, quick launches, testing concepts Hero campaigns, specific brand visions, complex scenes How to stage your products with AI using Photoroom The foundation of great AI staging is a good, clean product photo. So, make sure you have a clear image on a simple background that makes your product more visible, before heading to the AI product staging tool. For this walkthrough, I will be using the picture of a ceramic mug I generated using Photoroom’s product photography tool. Step 1 Sign in to Photoroom by going to app.photoroom.com . If you don’t have an account, it takes less than 2 minutes to create one. Step 2 Select AI Tools from the left menu bar and click on Product Staging to open the staging studio. If you do not see Product Staging , select the See all button in the top right corner to view a list of all available AI tools. Step 3 In the staging area, upload a picture of your image and select a size. There are three size options available currently: Square, Portrait (3:2), and Landscape (3:2). Click Generate. Step 4 Photoroom AI automatically generates two lifestyle/contextual images that fit your photo. Select the one you prefer and click on Use image. Make any extra edits you want and download your final image. P.S. Currently, you cannot prompt the Photoroom product staging tool for specific lifestyle photos, although the AI algorithm is highly intelligent and reads context accurately. However, if you want highly controlled results of your product in a particular background setting, you can use AI Backgrounds to generate very realistic images. Here are 50 AI prompts to help you get started. Common mistakes to avoid when using AI for product staging Here are some common mistakes people tend to make when staging products, and how you can avoid them. 1. Composition problems: This happens with over-staging and poor scaling . They make the product photos look fake and overwhelming to the customer. Keep your product as the "star of the show" with minimal supporting props, and ensure it's proportionally correct next to familiar reference objects like books or phones. Example: Don't stage your entire skincare line in one bathroom scene, or make a coffee mug on a table look the same size as the flower vase on the same table. 2. Inconsistent lighting: This is probably the most obvious giveaway that an image was AI-generated. It happens when your product photo was taken in bright, direct lighting, but you place it in a moody, dimly lit environment. The product ends up looking like it's glowing or floating. To avoid it, pay attention to the lighting style of your base photo and choose environments that match. If your product photo has soft, diffused lighting, pick scenes with similar gentle lighting. If you have crisp, bright product shots, go for well-lit, contemporary environments. Example: A yellow purse will look like it's glowing if placed in a dark room. 3. Context mismatch: This is when products are placed in spots where no one would ever actually put them. Like a heavy protein powder tub in an antiques library. Your customer should see themselves in the contextual images. So always ask yourself, "Would I actually put this product here in real life?" Example: If you're selling kitchen gadgets, stage them on kitchen counters, not bedroom nightstands. If you're selling workout supplements, show them in home gyms or modern kitchens, not fancy dining rooms. Where and how to use staged product photos to drive sales The great thing about having a library of lifestyle product images is that they're incredibly versatile. Here are the key places where they can make the biggest impact: Product detail pages: Your product pages are where buying decisions happen. Having 1-3 lifestyle images alongside your standard white background photos gives shoppers that crucial context. Pro tip: Put your lifestyle images second or third in your image gallery. Start with a clean shot that clearly shows the product, then follow with lifestyle images that tell the story. Homepage and category banners: Using lifestyle product images here creates an emotional connection right from the start of the browsing experience. Which option is more engaging for a homepage banner: a plain product photo of a water bottle, or that same bottle being used on a hiking trail with a beautiful view? The second one tells a story and helps visitors immediately connect with your brand experience. Social media content: Social media is a visual medium where context is everything and this is where lifestyle product images absolutely shine. They feel less like advertisements and more like lifestyle content that happens to feature your products. This makes your content relatable and increases your chances of engagement. Email marketing : When you're announcing new products or running a promotion in your newsletters, staged photos help your products stand out in crowded inboxes. They create desire in a way that plain product shots often can't. Paid ads: Scroll-stopping visuals are everything on social media. Lifestyle images tend to perform better because they blend more naturally into social feeds and create stronger emotional connections. They also give you a much wider range of creative options to test. You can show your products in different contexts to appeal to different customer segments or highlight various use cases. Is AI product staging right for your business? AI product staging is not the perfect solution for every single business in every situation. The great thing is, this doesn't have to be an either/or decision. Many brands are now using a hybrid approach. This means investing in a small professional photoshoot once or twice a year for their core brand imagery, then extending those assets with AI staging for everything else. AI product staging is typically ideal for: Small to medium DTC brands: If you're running a direct-to-consumer brand without a massive marketing budget, you can get the professional look of brands with 10x your resources, without the cost. Marketplace sellers: If you're selling on Etsy, Amazon, or other marketplaces, standing out is everything. High-quality lifestyle imagery helps your listings pop among the competition, many of whom are still using basic phone photos. Seasonal businesses: If you need to show your products in different seasons throughout the year, traditional photoshoots become extremely costly. With AI staging, you can place your summer dress in a beach setting now, then create fall imagery showing it layered with a jacket later – all without new photoshoots. Businesses with large product catalogs: The economics simply don't work for photographing hundreds or thousands of products in lifestyle settings. AI staging makes it feasible to create lifestyle images across your entire catalog. New product launches: When you're racing to launch a new product, getting photography scheduled can be a major bottleneck. AI staging lets you create marketing visuals as soon as you have a single product sample. There are still cases where a traditional photoshoot is worth the investment, such as hero shots that might appear on your homepage for months or in major advertising campaigns, or highly specific creative concepts that require precise control and interactions that can be challenging for AI to generate properly. The real benefit here is that AI staging gives you options. You can: Use AI staging for the majority of your product catalog Save your photo budget for truly special pieces or campaigns Test different contexts and settings before committing to a photoshoot Quickly create seasonal variations without additional shoots Create professional photoshoots with AI The bottom line is this: AI product staging levels the playing field. It gives small brands and solo entrepreneurs the ability to create the kind of visual content that used to require professional studios and significant budgets. Take one of your products and see what you can create with Photoroom's staging tools.

title: Should You Use Topical or Oral Finasteride for Hair Loss?
summary: Oral and topical finasteride both block DHT, but they differ in efficacy, absorption, and compliance. Learn which option suits your hair loss stage and concerns.
body_text: Back to blog Should You Use Topical or Oral Finasteride for Hair Loss? Both oral and topical finasteride block the hormone that shrinks hair follicles, but they don't work the same way. Here's how to choose based on your hair loss stage, side-effect concerns, and what the evidence actually shows. Dr. Dennis Porto Jul 22, 2026 · 7 min read The question most guys are actually asking isn't "which formulation exists." It's "which one do I need to stop my hair loss without messing with my body?" So let's get into it. The short answer For most men with androgenetic alopecia, oral finasteride (1 mg daily) is the stronger, simpler, more reliable option. Topical finasteride reduces systemic DHT exposure somewhat, which can matter if side-effect anxiety is a real barrier for you. But it comes with lower efficacy, inconsistent compounding quality, and it still gets absorbed into your bloodstream to some degree. The "topical is safe, oral is risky" framing you've seen online is overstated. Start a chat with Dr. Dennis Porto Free Describe your symptoms and get real medical guidance, on your schedule. Why does the route of delivery matter? Finasteride blocks the enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT (dihydrotestosterone). DHT is the hormone that shrinks your hair follicles over time until they stop producing visible hair altogether. Both oral and topical finasteride block that same enzyme. The difference is where the blocking happens and how much of it you get. Oral finasteride lowers DHT throughout your entire body. That means every follicle on your scalp benefits, including areas you haven't noticed thinning yet. It also means the hair surrounding your thin spots improves in quality and thickness, which makes the thin areas less obvious overall. Most people don't think about this. Oral finasteride doesn't just treat the problem zone. It raises the baseline everywhere. Topical finasteride works primarily where you apply it. It blocks DHT conversion at the scalp level, which sounds ideal in theory. In practice, some of it absorbs into your bloodstream anyway, so you're not fully avoiding systemic effects. You're just reducing them. Meanwhile, you're also reducing the scope of what the medication can do, because the follicles you didn't apply it to don't benefit. In my practice, oral finasteride consistently produces better results. Part of that is the whole-scalp effect. Part of it is compliance. A pill once a day is simpler than a messy topical application, and patients stick with it longer. Consistency is the most important part of improvement, and it's entirely under your control. Where this gets nuanced If side-effect anxiety is genuinely keeping you from starting treatment, topical finasteride is a reasonable way in. I've had patients who were so worried about changes in libido or sexual function that they wouldn't touch oral finasteride. For those guys, starting topical gave them a way to get comfortable with the medication. Some stayed on topical long-term. Others eventually switched to oral once they realized they tolerated finasteride fine and wanted better results. If your hair loss is early, maybe you're just noticing some thinning at the temples or the crown, topical can also make sense. You're not asking the medication to do heavy lifting, so the somewhat lower efficacy matters less. If your hair loss is more advanced and you want maximum effect, oral is usually the better call. You want systemic DHT reduction working across the entire scalp, and you want the compliance advantage of a once-daily pill. One more thing worth knowing: topical finasteride is compounded, and compounding quality varies a lot pharmacy to pharmacy. Different vehicles, different concentrations, different quality control. There's no FDA-approved commercially available topical finasteride the way there is for topical minoxidil. That variability is a real issue. I've seen patients who weren't improving simply because their compounded formulation was off. What to actually do If you're ready to start and aren't especially worried about side effects: oral finasteride, 1 mg, once daily. It's the most studied, most straightforward option. If side-effect anxiety is a real barrier: start with topical finasteride. Use it consistently. Reassess at 6 to 12 months. If you're tolerating it well and want stronger results, switching to oral is always on the table. If you're already on topical minoxidil: you can get finasteride compounded into the same solution, which adds a second active ingredient without adding an extra step. That's a genuine practical advantage. Regardless of route: give finasteride at least 12 months before judging results. Visible improvement typically starts around month 6. Month 12 is when it really becomes obvious. Quitting at month 4 because you don't see anything is quitting right before the payoff. Take a baseline photo in consistent lighting on day one. Compare at month 6 and month 12. Your mirror lies to you daily. Photos don't. When to ask a doctor about this specifically If you've read this and you're still not sure which route fits your situation, or if you've been on finasteride and you're not sure whether what you're experiencing is a real side effect or just normal day-to-day variation, that's exactly the kind of question worth putting in front of a dermatologist who prescribes these medications regularly. A real consultation with a real doctor, through chat, where you can send photos, walk through your history, and get a prescription if that's the right call. You start it from your phone whenever you're ready, and you'll usually have a response back the same day. Frequently asked questions Does topical finasteride completely avoid sexual side effects? No. Topical finasteride still gets absorbed systemically to some degree. The side-effect risk is reduced compared to oral, but it's not eliminated. The "topical is side-effect-free" framing that some brands use is misleading. How common are sexual side effects with oral finasteride? Rarer than the internet makes them seem. In clinical trials, decreased libido occurred in roughly 1-2% of men on finasteride versus about 1% on placebo [per Kaufman et al., J Am Acad Dermatol , 1998]. In practice, many patients who report side effects are experiencing normal day-to-day variation in libido or function and attributing it to the medication because they're hyper-aware. A doctor who knows these medications well can help you sort that out. Can I switch from topical to oral (or vice versa) later? Yes. There's no medical reason you can't switch routes. If you start topical and want stronger results, switching to oral is straightforward. If you start oral and want to reduce systemic exposure, switching to topical is an option too. Should I use finasteride and minoxidil together? They work through completely different mechanisms, so combining them often makes sense. Minoxidil stimulates hair growth directly; finasteride blocks the hormone that's causing the loss. They complement each other. Your dermatologist can help you decide whether you need one or both based on where your hair loss stands. Is finasteride safe long-term? Oral finasteride has over 25 years of safety data [per long-term extension data from Leyden et al., J Am Acad Dermatol , 2014]. It's one of the most studied medications in dermatology. Long-term use is well-supported for androgenetic alopecia, and side effects that do occur are typically reversible upon stopping the medication. Bottom line For most men losing their hair, oral finasteride is the stronger, simpler choice. Topical finasteride is a reasonable alternative if side-effect anxiety is a real barrier or if your hair loss is early. But the "safe versus risky" framing between the two is overblown. Both work. Oral works better. Consistency with either one matters more than which route you pick. title: How to Verify Employee Identity Online in India: PAN, Aadhaar, Voter ID & Driving Licence
summary: Learn how to verify employee identity online using PAN, UAN, Voter ID, and Driving Licence checks. Prevent hiring fraud with fast digital verification.
body_text: Insights & Resources How to Verify Employee Identity Online in India: PAN, Aadhaar, Voter ID & Driving Licence July 28, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet Why Employee Identity Verification Is Non-Negotiable in 2026 India’s job market is growing faster than ever, and so is the sophistication of identity fraud. According to a 2025 EY study on employment fraud, discrepancies were detected in 30 to 35 percent of resumes screened across industries. The BFSI sector alone saw a high incidence of employment history discrepancies, including inflated tenures, undisclosed exits, and fabricated past employers. For employers, the consequences of hiring someone with a fake identity are severe. A single fraudulent hire can lead to financial embezzlement, data theft, regulatory penalties, and even criminal liability under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023. The good news is that identity verification has become dramatically easier. Government databases for PAN, Aadhaar, Voter ID, and Driving Licence are now accessible through authorised digital platforms. What once required physical visits to government offices and weeks of waiting can now be completed in minutes. This guide walks you through each identity check, explains what it reveals, and shows you the fastest way to run all of them in a single workflow. The 4 Identity Documents Every Indian Employer Should Verify 1. PAN (Permanent Account Number) What it verifies: Tax identity, full legal name, date of birth, and PAN status (active, inactive, or deactivated). Why it matters: PAN is the most reliable single document for confirming a candidate’s legal identity. It is issued by the Income Tax Department and linked to the candidate’s financial history. Employers deducting TDS on salary must verify employee PANs, using incorrect PAN details can trigger mismatch notices from the Income Tax Department and attract a higher TDS rate of 20 percent under Section 206AA. What a PAN check reveals: – Full name as registered with the Income Tax Department – Date of birth – PAN status (active or deactivated) – Whether the PAN belongs to an individual, company, or other entity type Red flags to watch for: Name on PAN does not match the name on the resume or offer letter. PAN status shows as deactivated or inoperative (which happens when PAN is not linked with Aadhaar). Multiple PAN numbers associated with the same individual, this is illegal under the Income Tax Act. 2. Voter ID (Electoral Photo Identity Card — EPIC) What it verifies: Electoral identity, residential address, age, and photograph. Why it matters: The Voter ID is one of the most widely held identity documents in India, issued by the Election Commission. It provides an independent address proof and age confirmation that can be cross-referenced against other documents. Unlike Aadhaar, the Voter ID is not linked to biometric data, making it a useful secondary verification source. What a Voter ID check reveals: – Full name and father’s or husband’s name – Residential address as registered with the Election Commission – Age or date of birth – Assembly and parliamentary constituency Red flags to watch for: Address on Voter ID significantly different from the address declared by the candidate. Name spellings that do not match across documents. Voter ID number that does not return a valid record, this could indicate a forged document. 3. Driving Licence (DL) What it verifies: Transport identity, address, date of birth, and licence validity. Why it matters: A Driving Licence is especially critical for roles involving driving, delivery, field operations, or the use of company vehicles. But even for non-driving roles, the DL serves as a strong identity proof because it is issued after in-person verification at the Regional Transport Office (RTO). Verifying a DL also confirms whether the licence is currently valid, expired, suspended, or cancelled. What a DL check reveals: – Full name, date of birth, and address – Licence number and issuing RTO – Vehicle classes authorised (two-wheeler, four-wheeler, commercial) – Validity period and current status – Any endorsements, suspensions, or cancellations Red flags to watch for: Expired or suspended licence, especially for roles that require driving. Licence class does not match the type of vehicle the role requires. DL number does not return a valid record from the transport database. 4. UAN (Universal Account Number) What it verifies: Provident fund identity, employment history, and employer linkage. Why it matters: The UAN is issued by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and is linked to every PF account the employee has ever held. Verifying a candidate’s UAN is one of the most effective ways to cross-check their claimed employment history. Each employer they have worked with would have made PF contributions under this UAN, creating a verifiable employment trail. What a UAN check reveals: – Full name and date of birth as registered with EPFO – Linked PF account numbers – Current and previous employers who contributed to the PF account – KYC status (Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account linking) Red flags to watch for: UAN does not exist or returns no records, the candidate may have never been formally employed, which contradicts their resume claims. Employer names linked to the UAN do not match the employment history on the resume. KYC details under the UAN do not match the candidate’s submitted documents. Manual vs. Digital Verification: Why Manual Methods Fail Many small businesses in India still verify documents manually — asking candidates to bring original documents for physical inspection. This approach has three critical flaws: It cannot detect sophisticated fakes. Modern document forgery has become remarkably advanced. High-quality fake PAN cards, Voter IDs, and even Driving Licences can pass visual inspection. Digital verification queries the actual government database, which a forged document cannot fool. It is slow and error-prone. Manual verification depends on the HR person’s ability to spot inconsistencies across multiple documents. With hiring volumes increasing, the chance of human error grows proportionally. A digital platform returns results in seconds with zero subjectivity. It creates no audit trail. If a verified employee later turns out to have submitted fake documents, manual verification provides no defensible record of what was checked and when. Digital platforms generate timestamped reports that serve as compliance evidence under the DPDP Act 2023. How to Verify Employee Identity Online: Step-by-Step Here is the practical workflow for running all four identity checks digitally: Step 1: Collect candidate details. Gather the candidate’s full name, date of birth, mobile number, and the identity document numbers you plan to verify (PAN number, Voter ID number, DL number, UAN). Step 2: Obtain written consent. Under the DPDP Act 2023, you must secure explicit consent from the candidate before running any identity checks. Use a clear consent form that specifies which documents will be verified and why. Step 3: Choose your verification platform. You need a platform that queries government databases directly, not one that relies on visual document matching or OCR alone. The platform should support all four checks (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN) in a single workflow, so you do not need to juggle multiple tools. Step 4: Run the checks. Enter the candidate’s details and select the checks you want to run. A good platform will process all four simultaneously and return results within minutes. Step 5: Review the cross-record analysis. The real power of running multiple checks together is cross-referencing. Does the name on the PAN match the name on the Voter ID? Does the date of birth on the DL match the UAN record? Discrepancies across records are a stronger fraud signal than any single check in isolation. Step 6: Download and store the report. Generate a PDF report of the verification results and store it securely in the employee’s digital file. This report serves as your compliance documentation. What Happens When You Skip Identity Verification The cost of not verifying is not hypothetical. Industry data paints a clear picture: A single bad hire costs Indian companies between Rs 5 lakh and Rs 50 lakh when you factor in recruitment costs, training investment, lost productivity, potential legal fees, and the cost of re-hiring. For small businesses, this can be the difference between profitability and closure. Beyond financial loss, hiring someone with a fraudulent identity exposes your business to legal liability. If that employee causes harm, whether through financial fraud, data theft, or workplace misconduct and you failed to conduct basic identity verification, you can be held liable for negligent hiring. In regulated industries like BFSI, failing to verify employee identities can result in regulatory sanctions from RBI or SEBI, including fines and loss of operating licences. One workflow, four checks. Run PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN checks from a single candidate flow. No need to switch between tools or manage multiple vendor relationships. Cross-record confidence. ID Verify automatically compares names, dates of birth, and other identity signals across all returned records. You see at a glance whether the candidate’s identity details agree or conflict. No implementation required. There is no setup project, no API integration, and no sales call. Create an account, enter the candidate’s details, and run a check when you need one. Clear, downloadable reports. Every verification generates a structured PDF report that you can share with hiring managers, store for compliance, or attach to the employee’s onboarding file. Pay per check. No monthly subscriptions or minimum commitments. You pay only for the checks you run, making it ideal for small businesses and startups that do not hire at enterprise volumes. Start verifying your next candidate today at verify.salarybox.in Frequently Asked Questions Is online identity verification legally valid in India? Yes. Digital identity verification through authorised platforms that query government databases (Income Tax, Election Commission, Transport, EPFO) is legally valid and widely accepted. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 provides the legal framework for collecting and processing personal data for employment verification, provided you obtain written consent from the candidate. How much does online employee identity verification cost? Costs vary by provider and the number of checks. Basic identity verification (single document) can cost as little as Rs 50 to Rs 150 per check. Running all four checks (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN) through a bundled platform like ID Verify by SalaryBox is significantly cheaper than hiring a traditional BGV agency, which typically charges Rs 2,000 to Rs 8,000 per candidate for a comprehensive package. Can I verify employee identity without Aadhaar? Yes. While Aadhaar is a powerful verification tool, not all employees may be willing to share it due to privacy concerns. PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN collectively provide robust identity verification without requiring Aadhaar. ID Verify by SalaryBox supports all four of these checks. How long does digital identity verification take? Digital identity checks typically return results within minutes. PAN and Voter ID verification are near-instant. Driving Licence and UAN checks may take slightly longer depending on database response times, but are usually completed within the same session. Is identity verification enough, or do I need a full background check? Identity verification is the essential first layer it confirms that the person is who they claim to be. For most small businesses, running PAN, Voter ID, DL, and UAN checks covers the critical risk areas. Full background checks (employment history, education verification, criminal records) are recommended for senior roles, positions with financial authority, or roles in regulated industries. What if the verification finds a discrepancy? A discrepancy does not automatically disqualify a candidate. Minor differences, such as a slightly different name spelling across documents are common and may be resolved by asking the candidate for clarification. Major discrepancies such as a PAN that does not exist or a UAN showing completely different employers are serious red flags that warrant further investigation or offer withdrawal. title: Medical Spa POS Systems: A Complete Guide for July 2026
summary: This July 2026 guide covers medical spa POS systems, from EMR integration to injectable inventory, memberships, and HIPAA-compliant payment processing.
body_text: Your checkout process should take two minutes, but if your front desk is chasing down treatment notes, re-entering service codes, or digging through a separate med spa EMR just to close a visit, something's off. A well-built medical spa POS system fixes that by connecting scheduling, charting, inventory, and payments in one place. Whether you're comparing AestheticsPro pricing, looking up AestheticsPro reviews, or weighing options like Zenoti, Vagaro, or Aesthetic Record, this guide breaks down what actually matters before you sign anything. TLDR: A medical spa POS system must combine EMR, scheduling, inventory, and payments in one place to avoid billing errors and compliance gaps. Your vendor must provide a signed BAA, encrypted data storage, and PCI DSS-compliant payments, since a breach can cost hundreds of thousands in fines. Built-in injectable inventory tracking deducts units per treatment automatically, reducing product waste and shrinkage versus manual spreadsheets. Most POS migrations take four to eight weeks, with staff training running two to five days for core workflows. Decoda Health ties scheduling, inventory, consent forms, and payments together for independent elective-care practices with no per-provider fees. What Is a Medical Spa POS System? A medical spa POS system goes beyond basic payment processing. It combines transaction handling with scheduling, inventory tracking, patient records, and compliance tools built for elective-care practices. Unlike generic retail POS software, a medspa-focused system accounts for the clinical side of the business, connecting treatment documentation with checkout so nothing falls through the cracks between the treatment room and the front desk. Why Generic POS Systems Fall Short for Medical Spas Generic POS systems are built for retail: scan an item, process a payment, close the transaction. Medical spas operate on an entirely different model that requires consent forms, treatment histories, photo documentation, and HIPAA-compliant data handling baked into every patient interaction, all challenges unique to med spa practices . When staff jury-rigs a retail POS alongside separate EMR and booking tools, data lives in silos. Appointment notes don't sync with billing, and compliance documentation gets scattered across systems, creating audit risk and slower patient throughput. HIPAA Compliance and Your POS System Any POS system handling patient payments and records at your med spa must meet HIPAA requirements. That means encrypted data storage, role-based access controls, and a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) from your software vendor. Look for audit logs that track who accessed or modified records, automatic session timeouts, and secure payment processing that meets PCI DSS standards alongside HIPAA. According to HIPAA compliance guidelines for medical spas , a breach can cost a practice hundreds of thousands in fines, so verifying these features before signing any contract is worth the time. Core Features Every Medical Spa POS System Must Have Choosing the right system starts with knowing which features actually matter for a medical spa. Unlike standard retail POS setups, your practice needs tech that handles clinical workflows alongside transactions. Here are the core capabilities to look for: Appointment scheduling with provider and room management, so front desk staff can book, reschedule, and track availability without juggling separate tools. Patient intake forms completed before arrival, covering consent and health history tied directly to each client record. EMR and charting built in, covering treatment notes, consent forms, and before/after photo storage tied directly to each client's chart. Inventory tracking for injectables and retail products, with low-stock alerts to reduce waste and prevent running out mid-treatment day. Integrated payment processing that handles deposits, packages, memberships, and split payments at checkout. Reporting on revenue, provider productivity, and retention so owners can make informed staffing and marketing decisions. Membership and Package Billing Recurring revenue from memberships and packages is where many med spas leave serious money on the table. A good medical spa POS system should handle membership billing cycles automatically, track package usage per client, and flag when sessions are running low so your front desk can prompt a renewal before the client walks out. Look for software that lets you build treatment packages with different service inclusions, discount rules, and billing frequencies without needing a workaround every time. Injectable and Product Inventory Management Botox, fillers, and retail products require precise tracking to avoid costly waste or stockouts. A medical spa POS system with built-in injectable and product inventory management automatically deducts units used per treatment, flags low-stock thresholds, and ties product consumption directly to patient records. This gives you real-time visibility into your cost-per-treatment margins without manual reconciliation. Practices using automated inventory tools report measurable reductions in product waste and shrinkage compared to those relying on spreadsheets. EMR Integration at the Point of Sale The gap between the treatment room and the front desk is where billing errors live. When a provider finishes a session, the front desk should already see which services were performed, what products were used, and what consent was signed, all pulled directly from the chart, before the patient reaches the register. Without that link, staff manually transcribe treatment notes into billing fields, guess at service codes, or skip entries entirely when the waiting room gets busy. Those gaps quietly accumulate into revenue leakage and compliance exposure over time. True EMR-POS integration means consent status is confirmed before checkout opens, treatment-based billing auto-populates from the provider's chart, and the front desk closes the visit without chasing anyone down for details. Scheduling, Booking, and POS Integration Scheduling, booking, and payment processing need to work together without friction. The best medical spa POS systems connect appointment booking directly to client intake forms, consent documentation, and checkout so staff aren't toggling between disconnected tools. Look for automated appointment scheduling with real-time calendar sync, automated reminders, and the ability to collect deposits or process payments at booking. When these functions live in one system, front desk workflows move faster and clients experience fewer delays at checkout. Reporting and Business Intelligence Med spa owners often fly blind on revenue trends, provider performance, and retention rates without the right reporting tools. A good medical spa POS system should surface these numbers automatically, not require manual exports. Look for dashboards that track: Practice revenue analytics by provider, service, or product so you can spot what's actually driving growth Client retention and rebooking rates to gauge long-term practice health Inventory turnover to reduce waste and prevent stockouts on high-demand retail How to Compare and Choose a Medical Spa POS System System Built-in EMR Injectable Tracking Membership Billing High-Risk Payments Per-Provider Fees Support Model AestheticsPro Yes Yes Limited tiers No Yes Standard tickets Zenoti Yes Yes Yes No Yes Offshore, delayed Aesthetic Record Yes Yes Basic No Yes Standard tickets Vagaro Basic Basic Basic No Yes Standard tickets Decoda Health Yes Yes Advanced Yes No Sub-5-min Slack Front desk check-in and intake should work together so new patient forms flow directly into the appointment without manual re-entry. EMR documentation needs to support photo capture, consent forms, and treatment notes in one place. Payment processing fees compound quickly at scale, so confirm per-transaction rates upfront. Support quality matters more than feature lists when something breaks mid-shift. Switching POS Systems: What the Migration Actually Looks Like Most migrations take four to eight weeks depending on data complexity. The key steps are exporting client records, treatment histories, and payment data from your current system, then importing into the new one with a parallel-run period where both systems operate simultaneously. Staff training typically runs two to five days for core workflows. The biggest risk is data loss during the transfer, particularly for injectable medication records , so confirm your new vendor offers a dedicated onboarding team before signing. There are no per-provider fees that inflate as you grow, and onboarding is designed to get your team running without weeks of training. Final Thoughts on Picking a Medical Spa POS System That Works for Your Practice The gap between a generic POS and one built for med spas shows up fast, in billing errors, compliance gaps, and a front desk that never quite has the right information. Getting the right system in place means your team works from the same data every time. Book a short intro call and see how Decoda Health handles this for independent practices. Frequently Asked Questions What should I look for in a medical spa POS system that handles memberships and injectables? Prioritize software that connects membership billing, injectable inventory tracking, and EMR documentation in one system rather than across separate tools. You want automatic billing cycles, per-treatment unit deductions for Botox and fillers, and low-stock alerts — all tied to the patient record so your front desk and clinical staff see the same data at checkout. AestheticsPro, Zenoti, Aesthetic Record, and Vagaro each handle pieces of this differently, so confirm membership configuration depth before committing. AestheticsPro vs Zenoti vs Decoda Health for a med spa with memberships and high-risk services? AestheticsPro is described by many practice owners as dated — loyal user base, but limited flexibility for complex membership tiers or high-risk payment processing. Zenoti has broad features but generates consistent complaints around slow support and rigid workflows. Decoda Health was built specifically for independent elective-care practices and supports high-risk services like peptides, semaglutide, and TRT/HRT through its payment processing layer, which most legacy med spa software cannot do without a workaround. How long does switching medical spa software actually take, and will I lose my data? Most migrations run four to eight weeks depending on how much treatment history and payment data you need to transfer. A parallel-run period — where both systems operate at the same time — protects against data loss and lets your team train on the new system before fully cutting over. Staff training on core workflows typically takes two to five days. Confirm upfront that your new vendor provides a dedicated onboarding team, not just a help center and a ticket queue. What is the difference between a medical spa EMR and a medical spa POS system? A med spa EMR manages clinical records — treatment notes, consent forms, photo documentation, and patient history. A POS system handles transactions, packages, and checkout. The problem is that running them as separate tools creates billing errors, compliance gaps, and slower patient throughput. The best medspa software combines both so that consent status, services rendered, and products used auto-populate at checkout directly from the provider's chart. Can I find free or low-cost medical spa EMR software that handles scheduling and payments? Free med spa EMR options exist but typically lack integrated payment processing, membership billing, and HIPAA-compliant inventory tracking — meaning you end up paying for three or four separate tools to fill the gaps. For practices evaluating options like free aesthetic EMR software, the honest math is to add up per-transaction fees, separate booking software costs, and any add-on inventory tools before assuming free means cheaper. What's the best medical spa POS system for a single-location practice that wants to avoid per-provider fees? For single-location practices, the per-provider fee model quickly becomes expensive as you add injectors or aestheticians, so look for flat-rate pricing that doesn't penalize growth. Decoda Health charges no per-provider fees, which keeps your monthly cost predictable whether you have two providers or ten. Compare total cost of ownership — including payment processing rates, onboarding fees, and add-on charges — before signing any contract. How do I know if my current med spa software is HIPAA-compliant enough to avoid fines? Start by confirming your vendor has signed a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with your practice — without one, you carry the compliance liability alone. Beyond the BAA, your system needs encrypted data storage, role-based access controls, audit logs tracking who accessed records, and PCI DSS-compliant payment processing. A breach can cost hundreds of thousands in fines, so pull the BAA and run through this checklist before your next renewal. AestheticsPro vs Aesthetic Record — which one handles injectable tracking better? Both systems offer injectable tracking, but the depth varies considerably in how they tie unit deductions to the patient chart at the time of treatment rather than requiring manual entry afterward. AestheticsPro has a loyal user base but is frequently described by practice owners as dated, with limited flexibility for complex workflows. Aesthetic Record offers more modern UX but has its own limitations around membership configuration and high-risk payment processing, so test the injectable deduction workflow hands-on before committing. Can I build a functional med spa booking and payment setup without switching my entire EMR? You can layer a booking and payment tool on top of your existing EMR, but the gap between the two systems is where billing errors and compliance gaps live — services rendered in the chart don't auto-populate at checkout, and staff end up manually bridging the two. If your current EMR handles clinical documentation well but checkout is broken, a short-term patch may buy time. Long-term, practices that run scheduling, charting, and payments in one system consistently see faster patient throughput and fewer front-desk errors. What's the best EMR for Botox and filler practices that need per-unit inventory tracking? The best med spa EMR for injectable practices automatically deducts Botox or filler units per treatment directly from inventory when a provider documents the service, rather than requiring a separate manual entry. Look for systems where the provider's chart entry and the inventory ledger talk to each other in real time, with low-stock alerts before you run out mid-treatment day. Decoda Health ties injectable unit tracking to the patient record automatically, which eliminates the spreadsheet reconciliation most practices still do at end of week. Is Vagaro good for medical spas, or is it really built for salons and fitness studios? Vagaro works well for appointment booking and basic payments, but it was built for salons and fitness studios — not for practices that need HIPAA-compliant EMR documentation, injectable inventory tracking, and BAA coverage. Med spas using Vagaro typically end up adding a separate clinical charting tool and a compliance layer, which brings you back to a fragmented multi-tool setup. If your practice offers any clinical services like injectables, laser treatments, or weight loss programs, a system purpose-built for medical aesthetics will handle those workflows without the workarounds. How does AestheticsPro pricing work, and what should I expect to pay? AestheticsPro pricing is structured around subscription tiers based on the number of providers and features included, but public pricing isn't fully disclosed, and add-on costs for features like patient portal access or advanced reporting can raise your effective monthly bill. Before signing, ask specifically about per-provider fees, payment processing rates, onboarding costs, and any charges for data export if you decide to leave. Comparing the all-in monthly cost against alternatives like Zenoti, Aesthetic Record, or Decoda Health gives you a clearer picture than comparing base subscription rates alone. What questions should I ask on a medical spa software demo to avoid getting locked into the wrong system? Ask the vendor to show you the full checkout flow from a completed treatment note to a closed invoice — not just the booking screen. Confirm whether membership billing handles rollover credits, multi-tier discounts, and automated renewal without manual intervention. Get specifics on payment processing fees and whether high-risk services like peptides or semaglutide are supported. Finally, ask how you get your data out if you switch — vendors who hesitate on that question are worth approaching carefully. How does AI fit into a medical spa POS system, and is it actually useful or just a marketing term? AI in med spa software ranges from genuinely useful to purely cosmetic depending on where it sits in the workflow. Practical applications include ambient AI scribing that drafts a clinical note while a provider is still in the room, AI inventory photo upload that reads a packing slip and auto-populates stock, and an AI front desk that answers calls and books appointments when your team can't pick up. The distinction worth asking about is whether the AI was built into the system from the start or added on top of a legacy architecture — bolted-on AI tools typically can't act on data from other parts of the system the way a natively built one can. When does it make sense to switch medical spa software versus patching what you already have? Patching makes sense when one specific workflow is broken and a single integration can fix it without cascading into other systems. It stops making sense when your front desk is toggling between three or more tools to close a single visit, when compliance documentation is scattered across systems, or when your software vendor takes weeks to respond to a support ticket. The clearest signal to switch: add up what you're paying across all your current tools and how many hours per week your team spends bridging gaps between them — that math usually makes the case on its own.

title: What the GENIUS Act Means for API-First Fintechs
summary: Nov 14, 2025. GENIUS Act ushers in the era of regulated stablecoins. Here’s what it means for the industry (and how Coast customers are already ahead).
body_text: On July 18, 2025, the U.S. took a defining step in digital asset policy. With the signing of the GENIUS Act, stablecoins now have a federal regulatory framework for the first time. The implications are massive: consumer protections, AML enforcement, and reserve transparency are now federal requirements, not guidelines. And for companies operating at the intersection of stablecoins, APIs, and global finance, one thing is clear: 2025 is no longer a wait-and-see year. At Coast, we work with many of the world’s leading stablecoin players like BVNK , Rain and Mesh , and others. These companies aren’t just reacting to regulation. They’re setting the benchmark for how compliance is displayed and scaled. And they’re doing it with Coast. It’s go time. What’s in the GENIUS Act The GENIUS Act introduces the first federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. The law focuses on six core areas: 100% Reserve Requirements : Issuers must hold fully backed, liquid reserves - either in U.S. dollars or short-term Treasuries. Monthly Reserve Disclosures : Public, standardized reporting on reserve composition is now mandatory. Consumer Protection Rules : Marketing must be fair and transparent. Stablecoins may not be presented as legal tender or U.S. government-backed. Federal-State Alignment : Harmonizes state-by-state licensing into a unified compliance pathway.
